newsitem.title: MEXICO: Thousands flock to Mexico opposition rally.
newsitem.headline: Thousands flock to Mexico opposition rally.

text.p: An estimated 100,000 people poured into Mexico City's ancient Zocalo square on Saturday in a final show of support for opposition leader Cuauhtemoc Cardenas in next week's mayoral election.

Polls show the veteran opposition leader, founder of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), with a seemingly unbeatable lead over his nearest rival for mayor of Mexico City with a week to go before voting on July 6.

The vote is the first this century for the prestigious post, previously a presidential appointment, and will make the winner the most important politician in the country after the president, analysts say.
Organizers said more than 100,000 Mexicans packed the city center for the PRD's last main event before a ban on campaigning begins on Tuesday.
Waving flags and wearing T-shirts emblazoned with the PRD's yellow Aztec sun, they chanted their leader's name between fireworks and campaign songs.
"This campaign close is full of happiness and hope," Cardenas told the crowd.

Although the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has painted the PRD and its supporters as violent radicals, Saturday's crowd was mostly made up of middle-class professionals and their families.
Many middle class voters still hurting after 1995's economic crisis have deserted the PRI, in power since 1929. They have been lured by the PRD's promises of honest government and better wages.
"With this election the changes will be palpable," said accountant Roberto Monroy Ponce.
"He is offering us security, employment and better (city) services ... and he was robbed of the presidency in the past."
Millions of Mexicans believe Cardenas won the 1988 presidential vote but was denied victory by massive fraud.
Other Mexico City residents are simply fed up with years of official dishonesty.

"We motorcyclists are all sick of so much corruption, theft by the government and abuses by the police," said Bruno Pastrana, graphic designer and leader of a gang of bikers whose Harley Davidsons had been painted in the PRD's yellow.
Many of his supporters see this election, and Cardenas' likely victory, as a dry-run for the 2000 presidential race.
"If they can govern the biggest city in the world they can govern the country in the year 2000," said architect Juan Alvarado Mendes.
